text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated error-rate (502/504) for inference requests in us-east for the last 4m. Auto-routing falling back to us-west, then quickly to eu, creating traffic oscillation. See metrics: https://telemetry.redwood/graphs/2001239999
sam: acked. paging alex (oncall) @alex :pager:
alex: on it, looking at router logs now. initial hypothesis: healthcheck flapping between regions causing circuit to oscillate.
lee: seeing a pattern where us-east healthcheck probe returns 200 then 500 within 30s window. probing agent logs show intermittent auth timeouts to the health endpoint.
dana: customer-facing dashboards show a spike in request latency and 502s for a handful of enterprise customers in us-east. customers: acme-corp, finalpha.
alex: quick impact summary: ~6% of requests failing for those customers, but overall platform still serving via fallback. repeated fallback is increasing tail latency and causing cache thundering. severity: P1-ish (customer visible).
alex: mitigation plan: 1) pause auto-fallback routing policy for affected model families; 2) increase healthcheck stability window (from 3 -> 10s) and probe retries; 3) disable cross-region fast-failover until we confirm probe reliability.
morgan: should we run a canary to keep latency for high-SLA customers?
alex: yes — create an explicit route for the enterprise customers to pin to last-known-good region while we stabilize. using `redwoodctl routes pin --org acme-corp --region us-east --until 15m`
infra-bot: executed: `redwoodctl routes pin --org acme-corp --region us-east --until 15m` (cmd ran by alex).
lee: adding logs: healthcheck logs from proxy:``` 
[2026-07-08T14:12:03Z] GET /hc -> 200 (latency 45ms)
[2026-07-08T14:12:29Z] GET /hc -> 502 (upstream conn reset)
[2026-07-08T14:12:59Z] GET /hc -> 200 (latency 50ms)
```
dana: any config churn recently? I see a routing policy rollout around 14:08 by infra-deploy-bot. Could the new policy have different thresholds?
sre-bot: config change detected: `routing/fallback-policy v3.1` rolled at 2026-07-08T14:08 by infra-deploy-bot. New policy reduces healthcheck grace window.
alex: that matches. v3.1 made fallback faster to reduce p75 for low-latency traffic but didn't account for transient auth blips on east. reverting to v3.0 for safety.
alex: action: revert fallback policy -> `redwoodctl config set routing/fallback-policy=3.0 --apply`
infra-bot: started rollback of routing/fallback-policy to 3.0 (initiated by alex).
morgan: i'm going to take over the thread in 10m; alex, can you capture any remaining runbook steps and handoff?
alex: handing off. current state: pinned enterprise orgs to us-east, rollback started, autoscaling unaffected. healthcheck window bumped to 10s for us-east by temporary override. continuing to observe.
lee: note: during the oscillation, some requests were routed to a different model variant (model-x-small-quant) in us-west due to variant-fallback mapping; that increased failure rate for long-context requests. not sure if policy mis-map contributed.
dana: good catch — that would explain request-level 400s when long-context token count > 4k. need to verify variant mapping table.
alex: command to inspect variant mapping: `redwoodctl model-variants get --model model-x --region us-west`
infra-bot: response: model-x -> [model-x-4k-fp16, model-x-small-quant] mapping exists; fallback order depends on region capacity and variant-labels.
morgan: i'm on it. will validate mapping and add a temporary rule to prefer full-fp16 for requests with >2k tokens: `redwoodctl routing add-rule --if tokens>2000 --prefer model-x-4k-fp16`
alex: thanks. also temp disable cross-region fast-failover: `redwoodctl config set routing/cross-region-fast-failover=false --apply`
infra-bot: cross-region-fast-failover disabled (by morgan).
lee: after rollback and overrides, we see the error-rate drop back to baseline in us-east within 6m. fallback oscillation stopped.
dana: customer impact update: acme-corp reported degraded experience but no data loss. support notified: #support-notifications thread created.
alex: post-mitigation checklist: - keep overrides for 30m - run full config diff against v3.1 to find threshold that caused sensitivity - prepare postmortem and timeline - schedule rollback test in staging for v3.1 with simulated health jitter
morgan: taking over oncall for the next 2 hours, will monitor and escalate if anything recurs. alex dropping off. :thumbsup:
alex: handing off to morgan. leaving notes in incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/2001239999
sre-bot: Pager: alex acknowledged the incident and handed off to morgan at 2026-07-08T14:25:10Z.
pager: paging morgan (primary oncall) — please ack.
morgan: acked, monitoring dashboards closely. set an alert to notify if fallback count > 1 in 10m window.
lee: follow-up: I found an auth token rotation that occurred in the healthcheck proxy at 14:11 that briefly produced 401s for internal probes. will include in postmortem.
dana: CS/contact: outreach started to acme-corp and finalpha with ETA for resolution and follow-up.
morgan: current status: mitigated (oscillation stopped), monitoring for 40m. scheduling postmortem with stakeholders for 16:00 UTC.
alex: thanks team. add severity tag P1->P2 after 1h no regression.
morgan: noted. closing active pager at 2026-07-08T15:05:10Z if stable.
infra-bot: incident ticket updated: status=mitigated, runbook_ref=routes->fallback->v3-diff, postmortem_url=https://incidents.redwood/2001239999/postmortem
dana: schedule sent for postmortem.
lee: raw logs and healthcheck traces uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/2001239999/
morgan: closing notes: root cause preliminary: combination of aggressive fallback policy v3.1 + transient health-probe auth token rotation in us-east proxy -> caused ping-pong. contributing factor: variant-mapping allowed quantized fallback for long-context requests during failover, amplifying errors. mitigation: rollback policy, increase probe stability, pin high-SLA orgs, prefer full-fp16 for long contexts.
dana: thanks. will draft customer comms and include mitigation steps.
alex: good job all. postmortem owners: lee (tech lead), dana (customer comms), morgan (ops summary).
#end
